upstream.note: The revision every upstream citation below is a line number in, and the ref docs/PARITY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md pins. Cite it with the commit, not the tag: `git show <commit>:cmd/tailscale/cli/ip.go` reproduces the rows, and a reader who resolves a bare ip.go:113 against main instead will find something else there and read the audit as stale.

summary.note: Counted from the rows below and consistent with them: every `gaps` row has at least one entry in `findings`, every `faithful` row has none. This edition replaces the previous one, which audited PRs #293-#304 against upstream v1.102.3; these ten rows are the CLI parity ports merged after it, re-read against upstream v1.102.4. Three are faithful, seven carry at least one divergence, and ten findings are recorded. The previous edition's rows and findings remain in git history at 09409de.

auditedPrs.notes: The refusal itself is a correct port of switchProfile's matchProfile miss, and it happens before any teardown. But the resolver it makes terminal implements only two of Go's four matchProfile passes, so targets Go resolves are now hard failures; the refusal text also differs in case from Go's.

Test-only. The central claim checks out exactly: newUpFlagSet registers --nickname inside `if cmd == "login"`, so Go's `up` has no such flag. The replacement loop comment overstates upstream in the other direction.

Prefix of Go's sentence is now reproduced. The %s slot is filled with fork text rather than the OS, and the guard fires on every platform where upstream's fires only where HookNewBird is unset, so the ported refusal still does not match Go's output or Go's platform gate.

checkKubeconfigWritable, isWritable (directory probe by create+remove, file by O_WRONLY without O_CREAT/O_TRUNC), kubeconfigAccessErr wording, the MkdirAll-on-missing-parent arm with its non-NotExist early return, and the 0600 write all match upstream. Go's sandboxed-macOS arm is omitted with a stated platform reason (no sandboxed GUI build here), which is a legitimate gate.

Both refusals check out against serve_v2.go. The port check is inside the loop and ahead of the multiple-types refusal, and serveType's zero value really is serveTypeHTTPS, so reproducing Go's wrong-flag-name message is correct. \pL\pN is now the general category via icu_properties, matching validAppCap. Fixed iteration order in place of Go's random map order is disclosed and unavoidable.

Removing the invented --listen-under--cgi refusal is right: runWeb returns from cgi.Serve before it reads webArgs.listen. The --origin half replaces one set of invented refusals with a smaller set that upstream still does not have.

The masking rule and the join-every-offender behaviour match ToPrefs. The block it landed in is gated on a non-empty list rather than Go's nil check, and the check is applied to routes taken from existing prefs when the config names none.

The address arm is a faithful port of peerMatchingIP, including the st.Self pass and parsed comparison. The name arm is left as an exact, case-sensitive match while the code's own doc claims it is equivalent to Go's resolution, which it is not.

Test-only, no production change. The upstream facts the new assertions rest on hold at the pin: runWeb's cgi branch returns before reading webArgs.listen and emits nothing, so pinning empty stderr and exit 0 pins real upstream behaviour.

The `if !match` tail is ported correctly, family messages and all. The check that precedes it in the same function is still absent, so the no-address case keeps diverging, and runIP's --assert arm is unported.

gate.detail: Run on main at 7346530 (this branch changes only PARITY_AUDIT.json), CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, TS_RS_EXPERIMENT=this_is_unstable_software, toolchain 1.95.0 named explicitly because the box's default toolchain is a nightly with no clippy component. cargo fmt --all --check: exit 0. cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0. cargo build --release --bins: exit 0. cargo test --all-targets: FAILS, and the two causes are separate. (1) This branch's own: tests/parity_audit_ledger.rs holds this file to a contract, and its the_kubeconfig_row_writes_up_both_divergences_its_notes_name test hard-codes PR #296 from the previous edition, asserting it is still an audited row. This edition audits ten different PRs, so it fails; it cannot be satisfied without putting an unaudited verdict in the report, and the fix is a change to that test file, which this one-file branch does not make. The other five tests in that file pass, and satisfying them added the summary block and the @<commit> anchors. (2) Environmental, unrelated to this branch: tests::cleanup_refuses_live_socket in the tailnetd bin target panics at src/bin/tailnetd.rs:2311 with InvalidInput "path must be shorter than SUN_LEN" because it builds its UnixListener path under std::env::temp_dir(), 62 characters here, for a 107-byte path against darwin's 104-byte limit; with a short TMPDIR all four cleanup_* tests pass. Re-run with a short TMPDIR and --no-fail-fast, the whole suite is 1126 passed across 35 targets with exactly one failure, the PR #296 test above.

findings.title: Making the switch-target miss terminal exposes two unported matchProfile passes
findings.detail: Upstream matchProfile resolves a switch target through four passes in order: profile ID, NetworkProfile.DomainName, Name (the nickname), then NetworkProfile.DisplayName. resolve_target_to_id in src/ipn/profile.rs implements the first and third only, and says so in its own doc. Before this PR an unresolved-but-valid target was created; now it is refused outright, so `tnet switch <tailnet-domain>` and `tnet switch <display-name>` — both of which upstream resolves to a real profile and switches to — are answered with `no profile named "..."` and exit 1. The PR removed the fall-through that used to mask the missing passes without porting them.

findings.title: AdvertiseRoutes block gated on a non-empty list, not Go's nil check
findings.detail: ToPrefs guards the whole AdvertiseRoutes block with `if c.AdvertiseRoutes != nil`, so a config containing `"AdvertiseRoutes": []` sets mp.AdvertiseRoutes to the empty slice and mp.AdvertiseRoutesSet to true — it CLEARS the advertised routes. src/conffile.rs apply_to_prefs gates on `if !c.advertise_routes.is_empty()` (line 563), so an explicit empty array is indistinguishable from an absent field and the previously persisted routes stay advertised. A declarative deployment therefore has no way to stop advertising routes by editing its config; upstream does. The new masking loop was added inside this same mis-gated block.

findings.title: runIP's empty-address check, which precedes the ported `!match` tail, is still missing
findings.detail: runIP checks `if len(ips) == 0 { return fmt.Errorf("no current Tailscale IPs; state: %v", st.BackendState) }` BEFORE the -1 slice and before the match loop whose tail this PR ported. Two divergences follow and both survive the change. With no family flag, a node holding no address prints `(no matching tailnet address)` on stdout and exits 0 where upstream writes an error to stderr and exits 1 — exactly the script hazard the PR set out to remove, just in the other branch. With -4 or -6, the same state now reaches the newly added family message instead of upstream's state-bearing one, so the text is wrong where before both text and status were wrong. The commit body names this; it is recorded here because it is a live divergence in the function the diff claims to port.

findings.title: The name arm is not Go's name resolution, though its doc asserts equivalence
findings.detail: ip_arg_matching_node's doc claims the name arm is what Go reaches through tailscaleIPFromArg and that 'matching the name against the peer set directly is the same answer'. It is not. tailscaleIPFromArg matches a name with `strings.EqualFold(hostOrIP, dnsOrQuoteHostname(st, ps)) || hostOrIP == ps.DNSName` — case-INSENSITIVE on the hostname — then tries st.Self with the same matcher, then falls back to the host resolver. The merged code is `status.peers.iter().find(|p| p.name == arg)`: byte-exact, peers only, no self arm, no resolver fallback. So `tnet ip MY-LAPTOP` misses a peer upstream resolves, and this node's own name resolves nothing. The code comment makes the divergence harder to find than the code alone would.

findings.title: --origin gains validation refusals upstream does not have
findings.detail: Upstream takes --origin verbatim and validates nothing: runWeb does `if webArgs.origin != "" { opts.OriginOverride = webArgs.origin }`, and the sole consumer substitutes it for r.Host and string-compares it against the request Origin header's host. parse_web_origin instead refuses a value carrying a query, a fragment or userinfo, a non-http(s) scheme, or a leading slash, and rewrites an accepted value into a normalised `scheme://host[:port]` base. Every one of those refusals is a command line upstream accepts. It also trims before the empty test, so `--origin="  "` is treated as unset where Go sets OriginOverride to the whitespace. The PR's stated defect was refusing what upstream accepts; the refusal set is now smaller but not empty.

findings.title: The ported fatal still does not match Go's string or Go's platform gate
findings.detail: Upstream fatals with `--bird-socket is not supported on %s` where %s is runtime.GOOS, and only when `buildfeatures.HasBird && path != "" && !wgengine.HookNewBird.IsSet()`. HookNewBird is registered under `!ts_omit_bird && (linux || darwin || freebsd || openbsd)`, so in a default build on any of those four the flag is ACCEPTED and threaded into conf.BIRDSocket (tailscaled.go:813-814); the fatal is reachable only off that list. The merged refusal reads `--bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd (given "...")` and fires unconditionally, on Linux included. The stated goal — that an operator's grep or runbook keyed to Go's wording matches — is met only for the prefix, since Go's sentence always ends in a GOOS.

findings.title: Route masking is checked against prefs-resident routes when the config names none
findings.detail: ToPrefs applies `route != route.Masked()` to c.AdvertiseRoutes only — the config's own list, and nothing else. apply_to_prefs runs the check inside calc_advertise_routes over `prospective_routes`, which falls back to `prefs.advertise_routes.clone()` when the config names no routes (src/conffile.rs:504-507). A config that says nothing about routes can therefore be refused at daemon startup because of a route already persisted in prefs, where upstream loads the config and boots. Same block also prefixes each joined line with `config: `, so the emitted text is not upstream's bare `route %s has non-address bits set; expected %s`.

findings.title: runIP's --assert flag and its early-return arm are unported
findings.detail: runIP registers `-assert` (`assert that one of the node's IP(s) matches this IP address`) and, when set, scans st.TailscaleIPs and returns nil on a hit or `assertion failed: IP %q not found among %v` otherwise — before the peer/service resolution and before the match loop this PR re-derived. `tnet ip` has no such flag anywhere in src/bin/tnet.rs, so the arm is absent from a control flow the diff otherwise reproduces. Scripts using `tailscale ip --assert` as a cheap identity check have no counterpart here. The diff scoped itself to the `!match` tail, so this is a gap in the same function rather than a regression it introduced.

findings.title: The replacement loop comment overstates which flags Go registers on `up`
findings.detail: The PR split GO_UP_SPELLINGS to stop the file misdescribing upstream, but its new loop comment reads 'Every flag Go registers on `up` must get past clap' over a three-element list. newUpFlagSet registers roughly twenty flags on `up` unconditionally, and three of them — --audience, --client-id, --client-secret (up.go:104-106) — do not appear anywhere in src/bin/tnet.rs, so the invariant as written is false of this tree. The GO_UP_FLAGS doc comment, which scopes the set to 'the spellings a ported command line carries', is accurate; the loop comment beside it is not, and it is the one a reader of the loop reads.

findings.title: The ported refusal changes the case of Go's sentence
findings.detail: switchProfile and removeProfile both emit `No profile named %q` on stderr and exit 1. The merged refusal is `no profile named "<target>"`, lower-cased, matching this fork's existing delete_profile wording rather than upstream's. The stream and exit status are right; a case-sensitive grep keyed to Go's output is not matched.
